rfi.title: Punishing heatwave exposes cracks in France's nuclear power fleet
rfi.description: Three French nuclear plants halted production during this week's record-breaking heatwave as rivers became too warm to cool them, raising questions over the long-term future of Europe's biggest nuclear fleet.

rfi.title: Israel's targeting of Gaza's children proves genocidal intent, UN inquiry finds
rfi.description: The deliberate targeting of Palestinian children is central to a United Nations-mandated report's conclusion that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. The commission argues that children have not only been victims of the war, but have been targeted in ways that help establish genocidal intent. Israel has dismissed the findings of the report, released this week, as "defamatory".

rfi.title: France heatwave overwhelms hospitals and forces Pride march delay
rfi.description: Emergency doctors at one of Paris's biggest hospitals warned on Friday that wards had become dangerously overcrowded after a week of soaring temperatures, as authorities restricted public alcohol consumption, organisers postponed the annual Pride march and €130 million was pledged to help schools adapt to climate change.

rfi.title: Dembélé scores three against second string Norway as France claim Group I
rfi.description: Ousmane Dembélé rocketed up the World Cup goal-scoring charts on Friday with a hat trick as France demolished Norway 4-1 in Massachusetts.

rfi.title: Current Europe heatwave 'impossible' without human-induced climate change
rfi.description: A study comparing the heatwave that has swept across Europe this week with heatwaves in 1976 and 2003 has found that human-caused climate change is "unequivocally" responsible for the extreme heat over the last week – with France recording its hottest day since records began in 1947 on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Calls for child protection reforms in wake of schoolgirl Lyhanna's death
rfi.description: An investigation into previous child rape allegations against the suspect in the death of a schoolgirl in southern France has revealed failures by prosecutors and police. The case has unleashed a wave of criticism over how sexual and gender-based violence cases are handled in France, with victims, families and advocates pushing for reform.

rfi.title: Historic heatwave catches Europe's fashion industry unprepared
rfi.description: The most coveted accessory at the Paris Fashion Week shows this week was not a bag, a sneaker or a watch. It was an ice pack.

rfi.title: Paris court gives oil giant TotalEnergies deadline to tighten climate policies
rfi.description: A court in Paris ruled on Thursday that energy giant TotalEnergies must account for its consumers’ greenhouse gas emissions, giving the French company six months to adjust a legally mandated risk assessment.

rfi.title: France told to do more to protect children from human trafficking
rfi.description: France must step up efforts to prevent human trafficking and improve support for victims, particularly children and young people, the Council of Europe has said, warning that weaknesses in the country's child protection system continue to leave minors exposed to exploitation.

rfi.title: Pépé stars as Cote d'Ivoire beat Curaçao to reach knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Nicolas Pépé scored twice on Thursday to fire Cote d'Ivoire to the second phase of a World Cup tournament for the first time with a 2-0 win over Curaçao.

rfi.title: Relief in sight as temperatures set to fall in France after record heatwave
rfi.description: Temperatures are expected to fall in France from Thursday evening after another day of extreme heat that put 72 of mainland France's 96 departments on red alert, affecting more than 50 million people.

rfi.title: South African anti-migrant groups defend planned ‘Liberation March’
rfi.description: A coalition of South African organisations campaigning against undocumented migrants has defended its plans for nationwide demonstrations on 30 June, insisting the marches will be peaceful despite rising tensions and recent deadly unrest.

rfi.title: Kenya mounts huge security operation on Gen Z protest anniversary
rfi.description: Kenyan police put on a massive show of force Thursday in a bid to prevent protests marking two years since a landmark Gen Z uprising.

rfi.title: Macron to host Meloni in Antibes as France and Italy seek closer ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in the French seaside resort of Antibes, as the two leaders try to revive a relationship that has been marked by political differences.

rfi.title: Zelensky to miss Poland summit as Second World War row escalates
rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will not attend a major conference on rebuilding Ukraine being held in Poland this week, as a dispute between the two countries over Second World War remembrance threatens to overshadow talks.

rfi.title: South Africa beat South Korea to reach World Cup knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Thapelo Maseko scored mid way through the second half against South Korea to take South Africa into the knockout stages at a World Cup for the first time.

rfi.description: The European Union has moved a step closer to creating a digital euro, after members of the European Parliament passed a crucial vote on the virtual currency.

rfi.title: Brazil overpower Scotland to take Group C as Morocco wear down Haiti
rfi.description: Brazil outclassed Scotland 3-0 on Wednesday night in Miami to claim Group C at the 2026 World Cup. Carlo Ancelotti's men started the final round of games in pole position following their 3-0 win over Haiti on 19 June while Morocco edged past Scotland 1-0.

euronews.title: Frozen feasts and cool pools help Rome zoo animals survive heatwave
euronews.description: As a severe heatwave grips Italy, Rome's Bioparco is helping its animals stay cool with frozen treats, chilled pools and climate-controlled shelters while the capital remains under a red heat alert.

euronews.title: Small plane crashes into Beijing's tallest building
euronews.description: Police and emergency crews sealed off the area around Beijing's tallest skyscraper after a small plane crash damaged the building. Images from the scene showed a large hole in the upper floors of the 528-metre CITIC Tower, while witnesses reported seeing aircraft debris at the base of the building.

euronews.title: IRGC denies direct hotline with US, as Trump warns of ceasefire violations in Strait of Hormuz
euronews.description: The spokesperson for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) denied claims by American officials regarding the establishment of a direct hotline between Iran and the United States concerning the Strait of Hormuz, calling it a "sheer lie".

euronews.title: Venezuela updates earthquake toll: 920 dead, 3,360 injured
euronews.description: National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez updated the figure on Friday. The UN reports over 50,000 missing. Spain urges its citizens in Venezuela to contact consular emergency services.

euronews.title: France heatwave: baby dies in A&E, fourth child death this week
euronews.description: An 18-month-old baby died after being found unconscious with hyperthermia in a car on 23 June in Marseille, apparently forgotten by a parent on the La Timone medical campus car park while going to work.

euronews.description: The Qingdao Grand Prix opened with memorable performances as home favourite Wenna Zhuang delighted the local fans. euronews.description: The EU's Cypriot Presidency has successfully reached an agreement among EU countries that paves the way for talks between the European Parliament and the Council.

euronews.title: France heatwave: homeless people on the front line against the heat
euronews.description: With 61 departments still on red heatwave alert, people sleeping rough are among the most exposed. In Marseille, outreach teams step up to provide water, support and shelter.

lemonde.title: Au défi de la canicule, les urgences de Metz-Thionville s’attendent à un week-end « tendu » : « Désormais, nous recevons des victimes directes de coups de chaleur »
lemonde.description: Depuis trois jours, les passages aux urgences du centre hospitalier régional Metz-Thionville ont augmenté de 20 % et les appels vers le centre de régulation de 40 %.

lemonde.title: Les Etats-Unis annoncent des frappes en Iran en réponse à l’attaque d’un navire dans le détroit d’Ormuz, Téhéran réplique en visant des positions américaines
lemonde.description: L’armée américaine a dit avoir visé « des lieux de stockage de missiles et de drones » et « des sites radar côtiers ». Plus tôt dans la journée de vendredi, Donald Trump avait évoqué une « violation stupide » du cessez-le-feu après des frappes de drones attribuées à Téhéran.

lemonde.title: France-Norvège : les Bleus surclassent les Norvégiens grâce à un triplé de Dembélé et s’assurent la première place de leur groupe
lemonde.description: Kylian Mbappé et ses coéquipiers ont largement dominé, vendredi, les Lions norvégiens (4-1), qui se sont privés d’Erling Haaland. Les Bleus disputeront leur seizième de finale de la Coupe du monde, mardi à 23 heures.

lemonde.title: Séismes au Venezuela : le bilan s’alourdit à 920 morts, plus de 50 000 personnes portées disparues
lemonde.description: Les agences de l’ONU et d’autres organisations humanitaires ont réclamé un « accès humanitaire rapide et sans entrave », rappelant que des millions de personnes faisaient face à une insécurité alimentaire avant la catastrophe.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : dans l’Indre, François Ruffin se lance à la conquête des parrainages des maires
lemonde.description: Après Lyon, le député de la Somme a passé son « entretien d’embauche » auprès d’élus locaux afin de redynamiser sa campagne. S’il a été accueilli avec bienveillance, la question de la primaire et de la pertinence de sa candidature était néanmoins sur toutes les lèvres.

lemonde.title: Netflix, devenu un pilier de la création française, demande le « plafonnement » de ses investissements obligatoires
lemonde.description: La plateforme américaine alerte sur la « viabilité des règles actuelles de financement par les diffuseurs », qui lui demandent de consacrer 20 % de son chiffre d’affaires aux créations françaises et européennes. Netflix investit 250 millions d’euros par an en séries, documentaires et films français.

lemonde.title: Le Burkina Faso rompt avec la France, après l’adoption d’une résolution critique contre la junte au Parlement européen
lemonde.description: Le texte adopté le 18 juin par les députés à Bruxelles était porté par Christophe Gomart, directeur du renseignement militaire français jusqu’en 2017. Selon les informations du « Monde », les autorités burkinabées ont fixé à la France un délai de sept jours, à compter du 26 juin, pour fermer son ambassade à Ouagadougou.

lemonde.title: Les médias chinois muets des heures après le crash d’un avion biplace contre la plus haute tour de Pékin
lemonde.description: L’appareil a percuté l’immeuble en pleine heure de pointe, pour des raisons encore inconnues. Strictement contrôlée par l’Etat, la presse ne s’en était pas fait l’écho vendredi, alors que les locaux de la télévision nationale se situent tout près de la tour.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Volodymyr Zelensky affirme que « la justice pour l’Ukraine signifie également la justice pour le peuple tatar de Crimée »
lemonde.description: Le territoire, occupé par la Russie depuis 2014, a été placé en « situation d’urgence » au niveau régional par les autorités russes locales, pour faire face aux conséquences des récentes frappes ukrainiennes, qui ont causé des pénuries de carburant et d’électricité.

lemonde.title: En Tunisie, la militante des droits humains Sihem Bensedrine condamnée à 25 ans de prison
lemonde.description: L’ancienne journaliste est mise en cause pour son travail à la tête de l’Instance Vérité & Dignité, créée après la révolution de 2011. Sa condamnation intervient dans un contexte de durcissement de la répression des voix critiques en Tunisie.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : Gérald Darmanin a « perdu la confiance des magistrats », selon l’Union syndicale des magistrats, leur principal syndicat
lemonde.description: Le président du tribunal de Paris, Peimane Ghaleh-Marzban, a mis en garde les politiques contre des propositions « empreintes de simplicité et d’à à-peu-près ».

lemonde.title: Donald Trump menace de droits de douane de 100 % les pays qui mettraient en place une taxation des services numériques
lemonde.description: Ce coup de pression arrive au lendemain de l’accord formel donné par les pays de l’Union européenne à un accord commercial négocié en 2025 avec les Etats-Unis, qui prévoit un plafonnement à 15 % des taxes prélevées sur les importations européennes.

lemonde.title: OpenAI reporte son introduction en Bourse, sur fond de chute de SpaceX
lemonde.description: La start-up américaine d’intelligence artificielle aurait repoussé son entrée à Wall Street à 2027, selon le « New York Times ». Comme Anthropic, la firme voit par ailleurs son développement entravé par les restrictions imposées par la Maison Blanche.

lemonde.title: La Réunion s’alarme des ravages du « dou », une nouvelle drogue de synthèse, dans l’île : « Nous sommes submergés par ce phénomène »
lemonde.description: Les autorités s’alarment de la consommation croissante de cette cathinone de synthèse, qui provoque une forte accoutumance et de graves risques pour la santé. La préfecture lance un plan de 60 actions, dévoilé vendredi, intitulé « Zéro drogue. La Réunion dit non ».

lemonde.title: La Fonderie de Bretagne, reprise par Europlasma, va demander son placement en redressement judiciaire
lemonde.description: Le groupe Europlasma avait repris en avril 2025 le site breton, a enregistré une perte nette de 35,6 millions d’euros en 2025, plus de deux fois supérieure à celle de l’exercice précédent.

lemonde.title: EDF annonce la cession de ses activités EDF Power Solutions aux Etats-Unis et au Canada au fonds d’investissement KKR
lemonde.description: L’entreprise n’a pas précisé le montant de la transaction. EDF Power Solutions développe, construit et exploite principalement des centrales électriques renouvelables et des installations de stockage.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la fierté capverdienne portée par les Requins Bleus
france24fr.description:
🇨🇻 Après avoir tenu en échec l'Espagne et l'Uruguay, le Cap-Vert est à un match d'un exploit historique. Une victoire face à l'Arabie saoudite offrirait aux Requins Bleus une qualification pour les 16es de finale de leur toute première Coupe du monde.
 
À Santa Maria, Cece l'Anglophone, influenceuse nigériane installée au Cap-Vert, est allée à la rencontre des habitants, qui racontent avec émotion la fierté que leur inspire le parcours exceptionnel de leur équipe nationale.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : comment le Sénégal peut encore se qualifier en 16es de finale
france24fr.description: Après ses défaites contre la France (3-1) et la Norvège (3-2), le Sénégal a relevé la tête en infligeant une lourde défaite à l'Irak pour s'adjuger la troisième place du groupe I. Les Lions de la Teranga espèrent que ce sera suffisant pour être repêchés parmi les huit meilleurs troisièmes, mais il faudra pour ça une conjonction de scénarios favorables. Analyse.

france24fr.title: Canicule en France : la clim' est-elle de droite ?
france24fr.description: Considérée comme une aberration écologique par les uns, comme une nécessité par les autres, la climatisation est un sujet qui fait débat en France. Au Rassemblement national, Marine Le Pen plaide pour un plan massif de climatisation, une hérésie selon l’Insoumis Jean-Luc Mélenchon. La climatisation serait-elle donc devenue un marqueur politique ? Vouloir la clim', est-ce être de droite ? On en parle avec Philippe Moreau Chevrolet, professeur de communication politique à Sciences Po.

france24fr.title: En direct : les États-Unis frappent des cibles en Iran en réponse à l'attaque d'un navire

france24fr.description: L'armée américaine a annoncé vendredi avoir frappé des cibles en Iran en réponse à l'attaque par Téhéran la veille d'un cargo qui venait de franchir le détroit d'Ormuz. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Washington sanctionne le Rwanda accusé de faire de la contrebande d'or
france24fr.description: L'administration Trump emboîte le pas à l'Europe en sanctionnant Gasabo Gold, unique raffinerie d'or du Rwanda, accusée de faire transiter des minerais de conflit depuis l'est du Congo pour financer le M23. Selon Washington, les rebelles - qui occupent depuis plus d'un an les deux plus grandes villes de la région - achemineraient l'or vers Kigali avec le concours direct de l'armée rwandaise…

france24fr.title: Le Burkina Faso affirme "rompre ses relations diplomatiques" avec la France
france24fr.description: Le Burkina Faso, dirigé par la junte du capitaine Ibrahim Traoré depuis un coup d'État en septembre 2022, a annoncé vendredi la rupture de ses relations diplomatiques avec la France, accusée d'"activisme incessant" contre ses intérêts. Paris a répondu regretter une "décision hostile et sans fondement" et a ajouté que des "mesures de réciprocité qui s'imposent sont en cours d'examen".

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la France s'offre la Norvège et la première place du groupe I

france24fr.title: Cameroun : à Yaoundé, des milliers de ménages luttent pour avoir de l’eau potable
france24fr.description: Au Cameroun, l'accès à l'eau potable demeure un véritable défi pour des milliers de familles. france24fr.description: Comment donner plus de visibilité aux littératures africaines et afrodescendantes ? Critique littéraire, blogueur et fondateur du blog Chez Gangoueus, Réassi Ouabonzi est l'un des grands passeurs des lettres africaines francophones. france24fr.description: Alors que Donald Trump a menacé, vendredi, de frapper de droits de douane de 100 % les pays européens qui mettraient en place une taxation des services numériques, l'Union européenne a assuré en réponse qu'elle réagirait "rapidement et avec détermination".

france24fr.title: Au Venezuela, au moins 920 morts après le double séisme
france24fr.description: Les secouristes s'activaient, vendredi, au Venezuela pour retrouver les survivants du double séisme qui a fait au moins 920 morts, selon les autorités, et quelque 50 000 disparus.

france24fr.description: Israël, le Liban et les États-Unis ont signé un accord-cadre vendredi à Washington, sans en dévoiler le contenu mais avec pour objectif affiché d'ouvrir la voie à "une paix et une sécurité durables", selon le secrétaire d'État américain Marco Rubio.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Les supporters sénégalais font les calculs avant d’affronter l’Irak
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Mondial 2026 : le Sénégal doit impérativement battre l'Irak pour espérer poursuivre son aventure. phys-org.description: Uranus and Neptune remain two of the most mysterious objects in the solar system, primarily because they have been visited only by NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft in 1986 and 1989, respectively. phys-org.title: Proactive employees with high emotional intelligence do a better job, study finds
phys-org.description: In many organizations, large hierarchical gaps exist within work teams, raising the question of how frontline employees can strive for upward mobility in their careers. A recent study by the Department of Psychology at Lingnan University finds that employees who proactively seek opportunities, are willing to learn and, at the same time, have higher emotional intelligence carry out their jobs far better and are more engaged.

phys-org.title: Coal pollution reaches one of Earth's most remote mountain regions
phys-org.description: The Himalayas are often seen as one of Earth's great natural barriers, separating the heavily populated and industrialized regions of South Asia from the remote Tibetan Plateau. But new research, published in Geophysical Research Letters, suggests that this mountain range is not an impenetrable wall for air pollution.

phys-org.title: Why Ho Chi Minh City's pollution sources may have been misread for years
phys-org.description: Biomass burning, including the combustion of wood, charcoal and agricultural residues, is a major source of PM2.5, a fine particulate matter that degrades air quality and poses risks to human health. Much of this pollution is tracked by looking at levels of levoglucosan, a chemical that is formed when cellulose in plants is burned, from biomass combustion such as residential fuel use, cooking and open burning.

phys-org.title: Clean crystal surface lets single molecules hit ultimate quantum limit
phys-org.description: Scientists at the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light (MPL) have developed a technique for interrogating molecules on surfaces with spectroscopic precision, thereby reaching the ultimate quantum limit for the first time. With their findings, published in Science, the researchers open new opportunities for the study of molecule-surface interactions and molecular quantum technologies.

phys-org.title: Ocean warming above 1.5°C triggered year-round marine disruption across globe, study shows
phys-org.description: Researchers at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) led one of the first global assessments of how marine ecosystems responded during the first year when global temperatures temporarily exceeded 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

phys-org.title: Japan's small cities may face higher care burdens under the compact city policy
phys-org.description: As populations decline and age across the developed world, compact city strategies, which oversee the consolidation of urban facilities and guide residents toward transit-served hubs, have become mainstream policies. Yet most evidence about their benefits comes from cities that are already compact. Far less is known about the social costs that may arise during the transition to compactness in the small and medium-sized cities (SMCs) most exposed to shrinkage.

phys-org.title: ROS-producing enzymes guide plant cell division and tissue patterning, gene-editing study shows
phys-org.description: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) produced naturally during cellular metabolism often cause oxidative damage to cells. However, these molecules also play an important role in normal cellular signaling. While ROS are established as essential signaling molecules in various organisms, their precise role in basic plant development and morphogenesis remains unclear.

phys-org.description: A mission to raise the orbit of NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory is poised for launch no earlier than Tuesday, June 30, at 6:23 a.m. EDT (10:23 p.m. UTC+12), from Kwajalein Atoll, part of the Republic of the Marshall Islands in the South Pacific Ocean.

phys-org.title: Plasma and graphene combine to protect metal surfaces from corrosion
phys-org.description: Plasma is an ionized gas, often referred to as the fourth state of matter. Plasmas, which are created artificially by applying energy to a gas, are found in the fluorescent tubes that illuminate kitchens. However, they have many other possible applications, such as the production of graphene.

phys-org.title: Glass cells of atoms offer a new path to smarter, cheaper sensors
phys-org.description: More accurate navigation systems and improved wireless communications may not come from traditional electronics, but rather from atoms. Researchers at Penn State and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have developed a new way to build tinier, smarter glass sensors filled with highly precise and stable atoms.

phys-org.title: Hubble spies ancient 'Chandelier Cluster' forming stars in two bursts
phys-org.description: The subject of today's NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image is an ancient inhabitant of our galaxy. This sparkling scene features a globular cluster: a collection of tens of thousands to millions of stars, all tightly bound together under the influence of gravity. There are more than 150 globular clusters in our galaxy, though there may be others still undiscovered, hidden from view by dust or densely packed fields of stars.

phys-org.title: Beetle-like borings in 70-million-year-old titanosaur fossils reshape Lo Hueco fossil story

phys-org.title: NASA's PACE mission studies smoke and fires
phys-org.description: With the North American fire season underway, and a record number of acres already burned nationwide, NASA's Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, and ocean Ecosystem (PACE) satellite's three instruments are observing vegetation precursors to fires, along with plumes of smoke and their movement. These data will help scientists piece together clues that deepen their understanding of wildfires.

phys-org.title: Unknown 4,000-year-old stone circle in Belfast uncovered by archaeologists
phys-org.description: Archaeologists have uncovered an unknown stone circle that dates back at least 4,000 years to the Late Neolithic or Early Bronze Age and was most likely used for ritual activities.

phys-org.title: How atomic defects can program carbon quantum dots for future light-based technologies
phys-org.description: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are tiny carbon-based nanomaterials that have attracted increasing attention as environmentally friendly alternatives to conventional heavy-metal quantum dots. They are lightweight, photostable and potentially biocompatible, and their light absorption and emission properties can be tuned.

phys-org.title: Evidence identifies ancient Aboriginal mining in the Riverland
phys-org.description: Flinders University researchers, in partnership with the River Murray and Mallee Aboriginal Corporation, have found evidence that points to 7,000 years of Aboriginal mining of stone at Sugarloaf Hill in South Australia's Riverland. The dating formed part of the first detailed investigation into an Aboriginal chert and silcrete quarry in the Riverland region.

undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

proj-syn.title: Is a European Single Market for Energy Such a Good Idea?
proj-syn.description: Although textbook microeconomics shows why less energy-market fragmentation would be better for Europe as a whole, that does not mean it would be a good deal for countries producing low-carbon electricity at minimal marginal cost. In fact, if more integration creates free riders, the political backlash could be profound.

proj-syn.title: China’s Failed Rebalancing
proj-syn.description: When China’s leaders first acknowledged the need to rebalance the economy nearly two decades ago, it seemed like a matter of when, not if. But with the household consumption share of Chinese GDP remaining stubbornly low, officials’ promises to boost domestic demand have lost all credibility.

proj-syn.title: Crowning a Healthy Populism
proj-syn.description: Although recent political mobilizations in Hungary, Albania, and other parts of Central and Eastern Europe could be described as populist and nationalist, they have little in common with the aggressive ethnonationalism that MAGA professes. Could they be a model for a new form of politics?

proj-syn.title: Why Rules-Based Orders Fail
proj-syn.description: For a brief period after the Cold War, Americans persuaded themselves that the liberal order had become self-sustaining. And yet, any rules-based system elaborate enough to govern and interpret its own operations will eventually confront questions that its rules cannot answer.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.

proj-syn.title: Development in a Time of Disruption
proj-syn.description: Once firms and economies ascend to market dominance, they often kick away the ladder behind them and erect barriers to market entry to stymie would-be challengers. But developing countries can and do leapfrog incumbent technologies, and conditions for doing so may be particularly favorable now.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.
